title: Digital Flashpoint: AI And The Future Of US-China Crises | Hoover Institution
summary: A Hoover Institution panel discusses how AI shapes US-China competition, war-game findings on AI-enabled weapons, chip supply chains, talent and the risk of war over Taiwan.

RAND stresses that AI's strategic effect depends as much on adversaries' perceptions as on real capability: a tracking system need only be perceived as capable to be destabilizing.

CNAS argues the shift of military power into software could make rivals' capabilities harder to judge and change leaders' beliefs about whether they can win, raising the risk of miscalculation; it does not address US and Chinese views specifically.
